argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow certification theory, not a controls-cure theory. Aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents were recorded, and rollout includes an 8% initial exposure, rollback, and monitoring. The same record also shows the fraud dispute review segment remains below target and exposed, and the policy says that exposure keeps the disclosure duty in force absent approved risk acceptance. The supportable position is therefore to treat certification as compatible with explicit disclosure of the fraud dispute review limitation and monitored rollout, while avoiding any claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost override is claimed. The only governance-relevant efficiency point is that a caveated certification framing avoids unnecessary escalation if the auditor accepts that the packet is narrowing the claim to controllable launch plus required disclosure, rather than asserting full controls-based compliance.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not permit us to argue that small rollout percentage, rollback, or monitoring remove disclosure duties when the affected use case remains exposed. The admissible draft risk acceptance is not an approved exception and does not cover the fraud dispute review exposure. On this record, the defensible governance position is caveated compliance: certification can be defended only on the basis that required model-card disclosure is treated as a binding launch condition, not as an assumption that controls cured the weakness.
concessions: The current admissible record does not prove that the required model-card disclosure artifact already exists.
The current admissible record does not contain approved risk acceptance covering the exposed fraud dispute review segment.
A clean compliance claim would overreach on this evidence because the affected use case remains in scope for the initial cohort.
